claims.text: Adding 0.5-1 wt% graphene nanoplatelets to CoCrFeMnNi will reduce its coefficient of friction.
Adding 0.5-1 wt% graphene nanoplatelets to CoCrFeMnNi will reduce its wear rate.
The friction and wear benefits will persist from -20°C to 500°C, at sliding speeds of 0.1-1 m/s and normal loads of 10-100 N.
The graphene nanoplatelet addition will produce a thin, stable tribofilm containing graphene nanoplatelets.
The graphene-containing tribofilm will have low shear strength.
The tribofilm will prevent direct metal-to-metal contact.
Low tribofilm shear strength and suppression of metal-to-metal contact will reduce friction and wear.
The CoCrFeMnNi substrate provides high strength and toughness that support the proposed tribological response.
Relative to untreated CoCrFeMnNi, the intervention will reduce coefficient of friction by 25-45%.
Relative to untreated CoCrFeMnNi, the intervention will reduce wear rate by 45-65%.
The magnitude of the friction and wear reductions will depend on graphene nanoplatelet dispersion and stability in the HEA matrix.
The hypothesis can be tested by comparing the coefficient of friction and wear rate of graphene-reinforced and untreated CoCrFeMnNi against a steel counterface.
